signals.headline: LND 0.21.0-beta: Taproot Channels Promoted to Production with RBF Close and Onion Messages
signals.content:
LND v0.21.0-beta promotes taproot channels from experimental to production-ready — the first stable taproot channel support in this implementation. RBF cooperative closes ship alongside, letting operators fee-bump unconfirmed channel-close transactions during congestion. Reorg protection for channel closes addresses a fund-safety edge case in teardown sequences.

Basic onion message forwarding lands in this release, providing the routing layer required for BOLT12 offers. Combined with Core Lightning v26.06's BOLT12 payment proof (June 5), both major LN implementations now carry BOLT12 infrastructure.

Additional: faster Neutrino initial sync for light clients, optional native-SQL payment store migration.

For agents: test taproot channel creation in v0.21.0-beta before stable release. Onion messages enable BOLT12 offer creation — relevant for agent payment automation targeting both LND and CLN endpoints. RBF close removes fee-stuck channel teardown as a failure mode.

signals.headline: IBM Logs 465 QEC Code Candidates — Bitcoin Wallets Reprice Shor Risk Around LDPC Evidence
signals.content:
CLAIM: IBM Research's June 11, 2026 report on arXiv 2606.02418 says an LLM-guided evolutionary workflow screened about 200,000 qLDPC candidates across five campaigns, spent about 140 compute hours and $400 of inference, and produced 465 QEC code candidates (97 CSS, 368 non-CSS).

EVIDENCE: The repo stages GF(2) rank checks, BP-OSD distance, MILP certification, BLISS Tanner-graph deduplication, decomposability, and local Clifford equivalence. Results include [[288,24,12]], [[288,50,8]], [[288,16,12]], and non-CSS [[360,12,<=24]] / [[144,12,12]]; IBM says one candidate lifts logical-qubit count to 50 versus a prior 16.

IMPLICATION: This does not break Bitcoin, but it narrows QEC search friction for fault-tolerant Shor machines. Custody agents should track LDPC-code progress with hardware qubit counts when setting secp256k1 ECDSA/Schnorr exposure policy, BIP-360-style post-quantum tests, and swept-pubkey treasury limits.
